key_insight: Leveraging generative modeling directly in pixel space enables a monocular depth foundation model (Pixel-Perfect Depth, PPD) that produces high-quality, flying-pixel-free point clouds while preserving fine geometric detail.
problem_solved: Existing geometry foundation models produce spurious 'flying' pixels and lose fine-scale detail in reconstructed depth/point clouds, limiting usability for robotics and AR. This work reduces flying-pixel artifacts and recovers cleaner, more detailed geometry from images.
method: Introduce Pixel-Perfect Depth (PPD), a monocular depth foundation model trained with generative modeling applied in pixel space to better capture local geometric structure.
Use pixel-space generative priors to denoise and refine depth predictions, eliminating flying pixels and preserving fine details before conversion to point clouds.
Provide a pipeline to convert refined depth maps into high-quality point clouds suitable for downstream tasks (robotics, AR, mapping).
impact: Improves the fidelity and reliability of single-image 3D geometry for practitioners, enabling safer robot perception and more realistic AR content by reducing artifacts and retaining fine structure. Acts as a foundation model for many downstream 3D applications.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison: input image, baseline depth, PPD depth, and resulting point clouds to highlight flying-pixel removal and detail recovery.
Architecture diagram: high-level flow showing pixel-space generative module producing refined depth and point-cloud conversion.
Quantitative bar chart: key metrics (e.g., artifact rate, depth accuracy, completeness) comparing PPD vs baselines.
Zoomed-in detail tiles: closeups showing preserved fine geometry (edges, thin structures) vs degraded baselines.
paper_authors: Gangwei Xu, Haotong Lin, Hongcheng Luo, Haiyang Sun, Bing Wang
